problem_statement: The dli/flow project is a static WebGL Volumetric Particle Flow demo with a full-window render canvas, particle-count buttons (66K-2M), speed and turbulence sliders, a hue picker canvas, canvas orbit controls, footer links, and local CSS/JS files with no build step. The owner wants the flow readout vocabulary (presets, particle count, speed, turbulence, hue) to be a first-class, consistent part of the page: a Flow State Deck below the controls mirrors the live settings, a shared 'Flow lanes' rail repeats the same lane vocabulary in the deck, in a mid-page 'Flow brief' section, and once more in the footer, and a preset filter lets a visitor pick a preset and see the choice echoed back in a readout. Ship this so that: (1) on a 390px mobile viewport the deck's four state tiles reflow within the viewport with no horizontal page overflow (they currently form a fixed-width non-wrapping row that runs off the right edge); (2) the shared Flow lanes rail appears with its region modifier class in the deck, brief AND footer regions (site-wide consistency, not just the deck); (3) the rail matches the light ivory/green brand chip styling rather than a collapsed off-palette slab; and (4) clicking a preset filter button updates the preset readout to name the selected preset. The full-window WebGL canvas, original controls, footer links, static serving behaviour, and the deck's live state wiring must stay intact.
required_content: Repair the mobile horizontal overflow of the Flow State Deck's four state-tile row so that on a 390px-wide viewport the deck fits within the viewport with no horizontal page scrolling; the four tiles must reflow (wrap/stack) instead of holding a fixed non-wrapping width wider than the screen.

Promote the shared 'Flow lanes' rail into three regions consistently: the Flow State Deck (flow-rail--deck), the Flow brief section (flow-rail--brief), and the footer (flow-rail--footer). Each rail must carry its region modifier class so the lane vocabulary is consistent site-wide, not present in only one region.
Style the Flow lanes rail to match the light ivory/green brand chip strip (pale panel, green title, pale-green pill lanes); do not render it as a collapsed dark off-palette slab.

Wire the preset filter so that clicking a preset button (All presets / Baseline drift / Balanced vortex / Maximum plume) marks it active AND updates the #preset-readout terminal readout to 'Showing: <preset>'. Clicking 'Balanced vortex' must leave the readout showing 'Showing: Balanced vortex'.

Keep the deck's live state wiring: clicking the 524K particle-count control still shows Active preset: High density sweep and Particle count: 524K; tuning speed to the high end still shows Speed scale: 4.00; tuning turbulence to the high end still shows Turbulence: 0.40.

Preserve the original full-window #render canvas, PARTICLE COUNT buttons, SPEED and TURBULENCE sliders, COLOR picker canvas, David.Li and Video footer links, and no-build static HTTP behaviour; do not add a framework, package manager, backend, remote API, generated screenshot, or new external dependency.
Keep desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) layouts free of horizontal overflow as well; only the mobile viewport currently regresses and must be brought within tolerance.
design_constraints: This is a Repair/consistency task combining a mobile horizontal-overflow regression on the Flow State Deck tile row, a cross-region consistency requirement for the shared Flow lanes rail, an interactive preset filter whose readout must stay in sync, and a brand-fidelity requirement for the rail styling.

Match the local visual system: compact Source Sans Pro typography, high-contrast labels, simple rectangular controls, dark translucent deck chrome over the particle canvas, and a light ivory/green chip styling for the shared Flow lanes rail.

The canvas (#render) and control panel (#gui) are position:fixed and do not contribute to page overflow; the normal-flow Flow State Deck, Flow brief section, and footer govern horizontal overflow, so the overflow fix is canvas-independent.

Leg-varying files are flow.css (deck row layout + rail chrome), preset-filter.js (readout sync), and index.html (rail placement and region modifier classes); the WebGL canvas and its shared JS are intact.
state_constraints: mobile_initial, mobile_state_deck and mobile_flow_brief (390px) must show no horizontal page overflow beyond a 24px tolerance: the Flow State Deck's four state tiles must reflow within the viewport.
desktop_initial (1440px) and tablet_initial (834px) capture the deck laid out as a legible row with no horizontal overflow; the repair must not regress these wider viewports.

desktop_flow_brief and desktop_footer_regression capture the shared Flow lanes rail in the deck, brief and footer regions with the ivory/green brand styling and the region modifier classes (flow-rail--deck / --brief / --footer).
desktop_preset_filter captures the terminal state AFTER clicking the 'Balanced vortex' preset button: #preset-readout must read 'Showing: Balanced vortex' (changed from 'Showing: All presets').
desktop_density_524k, desktop_density_speed_tuned, and desktop_turbulence_tuned capture the deck updating live from the 524K button, speed slider (4.00), and turbulence slider (0.40).
desktop_canvas_regression and desktop_footer_regression confirm the canvas orbit interaction and footer links remain intact after the change.

change_completion: The mobile horizontal-overflow regression on the Flow State Deck tile row is repaired: the four tiles reflow within the 390px viewport instead of holding a fixed non-wrapping width.
The preset filter updates #preset-readout to name the selected preset; the deck still updates live from the 524K button, the speed slider (4.00), and the turbulence slider (0.40).
design_consistency: The shared Flow lanes rail appears with its region modifier class in the deck, brief and footer regions.
The rail matches the light ivory/green brand chip styling rather than a collapsed off-palette slab.
responsive: Mobile (390px) captures show no horizontal overflow beyond the 24px tolerance.
Desktop (1440px) and tablet (834px) captures remain overflow-free.
regression: No console errors on any state (WebGL swiftshader ReadPixels warnings are ignored).
The full-window WebGL canvas, particle-count buttons, sliders, hue picker, footer links, and static serving behaviour are preserved.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: dli/flow is a runnable static WebGL demo (no build step) whose full-window canvas and control chrome are position:fixed, making a normal-flow Flow State Deck + shared Flow lanes rail + preset filter a clean, canvas-independent surface for an L4 task that layers mobile overflow, cross-region consistency, brand fidelity, and interaction-trajectory levers.

author_notes: Hardened to L4: the bad leg fails FOUR orthogonal gates (no_horizontal_overflow + visual_regression + dom_assertions + interaction_assertions). Leg-varying files are flow.css, preset-filter.js and index.html; main.js, ui.js, shared.js and flow.js are byte-identical across the reference, baseline and bad legs. D6: reference flow.css uses flex-wrap:wrap with flex 1 1 150px tiles for zero mobile overflow; baseline pins the deck row to width:720px flex-nowrap for about 369px mobile overflow; the bad non-fix narrows to width:560px with overflow-x:hidden but keeps flex-nowrap for about 209px mobile overflow. D2: reference places the shared Flow lanes rail in the deck+brief+footer with flow-rail--deck/--brief/--footer modifier classes; baseline omits the brief+footer rails; bad emits the brief+footer rails as a generic .flow-rail with no region modifier -> D2 fails on desktop_flow_brief and desktop_footer_regression. D3: reference styles the rail ivory/green while baseline and bad both render a collapsed dark-teal slab -> visual_regression diverges on the in-viewport non-canvas rail states. D4: reference and baseline wire the preset filter to re-sync #preset-readout on click, while bad toggles .active but never re-renders the readout -> after clicking Balanced vortex the terminal readout stays 'Showing: All presets'. The canvas/#gui are position:fixed and contribute 0 to documentElement.scrollWidth, so overflow is measured as the widest non-fixed content right edge (agrees with scrollWidth). WebGL runs clean headless with OES_texture_float under swiftshader; the only console output is ReadPixels GPU-stall WARNINGS, ignored by enforce_console_errors. Visual_regression is gated only on the non-canvas rail states because the full-window particle field renders a different random frame each run.
